core_obligations: Show that for a coherent O_X-module F flat over the valuation ring R with dim Supp(F_K) at most r, the closed-fibre support has dimension at most r and sp_{X/R}([F_K]_r) = [F_kappa]_r (proof lines 427-456). First, the dimension statement is more-morphisms-lemma-relative-dimension-support-flat (tag 0H3X) (proof lines 428-429). Second, fix x a generic point of an integral closed subscheme Z of X_kappa of dimension r and compare the coefficients of [Z] on both sides: set A = O_{X,x} and M = F_x, a finite A-module flat over R; for a uniformizer pi with A/pi A = O_{X_kappa, x}, the additivity lemma chow-lemma-additivity-divisors-restricted (tag 02QG) gives sum over minimal primes q_i of Supp(M) of length_A(A/(pi, q_i)) times length_{A_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) = length_A(M/pi M) (proof lines 430-448). Third, since pi is a nonzerodivisor on M by flatness over R, pi lies in none of the q_i, so these primes correspond exactly to the generic points y_i of Supp(F_K) that specialize to x, and the displayed sum is precisely the coefficient of [Z] in the specialization sp_{X/R}([F_K]_r); meanwhile length_A(M/pi M) is the coefficient of [Z] in [F_kappa]_r by the definition of the cycle class of a coherent sheaf, so the two coefficients agree and the proof is complete (proof lines 449-455).
proof_roadmap: Dimension bound on the closed-fibre support from the relative dimension lemma for flat modules (proof lines 428-429).
Coefficient comparison at a generic point: unfold the coherent-sheaf cycle classes and apply the restricted-divisor additivity lemma with the uniformizer (proof lines 430-448).
Flatness makes the uniformizer a nonzerodivisor so the minimal primes are the specializing generic points of the generic-fibre support; both coefficients agree (proof lines 449-455).
